note: Possible flooding mechanisms and cause-matched investigative actions (Causal Diagnosis Addendum). These are hypotheses to investigate, not a hydraulic diagnosis. 'source_id' values must exist in sources.json.

mechanisms.label: Coastal overtopping / overland inflow
mechanisms.description: Sea water flows over the shoreline or through low openings and travels overland onto the road.
supported_by: Modelled or observed coastal flood extent over the corridor
mechanisms.does_not_prove: A flood polygon over the road does not show where water enters at road scale.
unknowns: Shoreline / edge elevations along the pathway (survey, vertical datum)
Which opening or low point admits the water
Whether the corridor floods before or after adjacent shoreline overtops

actions.name: Survey the shoreline edge and suspected entry pathway
actions.applicable_if: Coastal flood extent or documented pathway reaches the corridor.
actions.could_fail: Survey misses a pathway that only activates at higher water levels.
downstream_checks: Confirm pathway against historical high-water marks (USGS 2018) where available

actions.name: Evaluate continuous coastal protection (berm, wall, raised road) only where overland entry is demonstrated
actions.applicable_if: Survey shows overland entry along a definable alignment that ties into high ground.
actions.could_fail: Water enters around the ends; outfalls behind the barrier still back up at high tide (see BWSC adaptation scenarios).
downstream_checks: Check drainage behind the barrier at high tide

mechanisms.label: High tide blocking stormwater discharge / backflow
mechanisms.description: When the receiving water is high, outfalls cannot drain by gravity; stormwater backs up through the drain system and ponds on the street.
supported_by: Outfall location, invert elevation and ownership
Flooding that coincides with high tide and rain
mechanisms.does_not_prove: High tide alone does not show that a specific outfall is failing.
unknowns: Which outfall(s) serve the corridor inlets and who owns them
Outfall invert elevations vs tide levels (datum)
Whether tide gates / check valves exist and work
Timing of past flooding vs tide and rainfall

actions.name: Trace corridor inlets to their outfall(s) and confirm owner
actions.applicable_if: Always, before any outfall or tide-gate proposal.
actions.could_fail: Records incomplete; non-Commission outfalls are outside the BWSC model.
downstream_checks: Request drainage plans from the identified owner

actions.name: Compare reported flooding dates against tide and rainfall records
actions.applicable_if: Dated flood reports exist for the corridor.
actions.could_fail: Report dates are case-open times, not flood times; rainfall gauge may be distant.
downstream_checks: NOAA tide gauge 8443970 for water level; NOAA Atlas 14 for rainfall frequency context

actions.name: Review tide gate / backflow control, storage or pumping at the outfall
actions.applicable_if: Outfall is identified and tide-constrained discharge is shown by timing or modelling.
actions.could_fail: Storage or pumping undersized; gate closed during rain with no relief; power failure.
downstream_checks: Upstream ponding when the gate is closed
quote_inputs: Required storage volume or pump rate

mechanisms.label: Localized inlet obstruction / debris
mechanisms.description: Catch basins or grates are blocked by debris, sediment, leaves or snow so water cannot enter the drain.
supported_by: Repeated catch-basin reports at the same location
Maintenance or closure notes recording debris removal
mechanisms.does_not_prove: A 311 report is an allegation, not a confirmed blockage; the BWSC model does not represent individual clogged basins.
unknowns: Current condition of the corridor catch basins
Whether reported ponding cleared after cleaning

actions.name: Inspect and, if blocked, clean the corridor catch basins
actions.applicable_if: Catch-basin reports or debris notes near the corridor.
actions.could_fail: Flooding persists after cleaning, pointing to capacity or tide causes instead.
downstream_checks: Record whether ponding recurs after cleaning
Report to the asset owner, not by default to BWSC

actions.name: CCTV the connecting pipe if cleaning does not restore drainage
actions.applicable_if: Basins clean but water still not draining.
actions.could_fail: Defect lies further downstream or at the outfall.
downstream_checks: Follow to the next structure / outfall

mechanisms.label: Insufficient storm-drain or inlet capacity
mechanisms.description: Inlets or pipes cannot carry the rainfall runoff reaching them even when clear.
supported_by: Verified pipe sizes and hydraulic calculations
Repeated ponding during intense rain with clean inlets
mechanisms.does_not_prove: Road width or a flood footprint does not reveal underground capacity.
unknowns: Design storm used for the existing system

actions.name: Drainage capacity assessment (inlets and pipes) with the owner's records
actions.applicable_if: Ponding recurs with clean inlets during rainfall.
actions.could_fail: Records missing; tailwater (tide) controls rather than pipe size.
downstream_checks: Use practitioner drainage guidance (MassDOT PDDG Ch. 8)
Check impacts away from the site

actions.name: Added / relocated inlets, storage or green infrastructure
actions.could_fail: Moves water to a downstream bottleneck.

mechanisms.label: Unfavorable street grading / ponding
mechanisms.description: Surface low points or grades direct runoff to places without adequate inlets.
mechanisms.does_not_prove: A low point alone does not prove deficient drainage, and regrading can push water elsewhere.
unknowns: Validated surface elevations along the corridor (from Person 2 / survey)
Inlet positions relative to low points

actions.name: Topographic survey of gutters, low points and inlet positions
actions.applicable_if: Ponding is localized to a repeatable spot.
actions.could_fail: LiDAR resolution insufficient at curb scale.
downstream_checks: Check where redirected water would go

mechanisms.label: Multiple simultaneous causes / unresolved
mechanisms.description: Rain, tide and coastal inflow may combine, or available evidence does not discriminate between causes.
supported_by: More than one mechanism with supporting evidence
mechanisms.does_not_prove: Never force one causal label just to populate an answer.
unknowns: Owner records for all drainage assets

actions.name: Convene asset owners and collect drainage records before choosing a measure
actions.applicable_if: Two or more mechanisms are possible or ownership is split.
downstream_checks: Hydraulic modelling once records are assembled
